Chris — great, thanks for the diagram. Marcus and Laura are copied for the deep network and on-prem details. A few items we want to confirm before the sync so we can bring the right runbooks to the call: 

1) Preferred connectivity mode: VPC peering (full route exchange) OR PrivateLink/endpoint (proxy-style). If you lean PrivateLink, we need to know whether your side can host an NLB in front of the peer.

2) Certificate management for management API: will Pegasus provision a SAN certificate for the appliance hostname, or should Redwood provide a CSR flow? If you prefer the CSR flow, we will need an owner for the cert rotation runbook.

3) On-prem package sizing and host requirements: the spec we attached lists minimums (8 vCPU, 64GB RAM, 200GB SSD). Can you confirm the appliance node count and whether HA is required for the initial staging cluster?

4) Egress allowlist: already saw the file you shared. For staging we can rely on FQDN allowlist; for production we will provide static egress IPs. 

Attachments referenced: pegasus_network_diagram.pdf, redwood_onprem_package_specs.pdf

Laura, Marcus — can you add the preliminary firewall ports and an abbreviated checklist (3-5 items) we can hand to the Pegasus infra team before the sync?

Best,
David

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@pegasus-med.com>, Emily Park <emily.park@pegasus-med.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff and connectivity plan — firewall/ports checklist

Hi all,

Quick checklist for Pegasus infra team to validate before we schedule the appliance install window: 

- Management plane (port 443 TLS)
  - Allow inbound from Pegasus DMZ to appliance management IP on TCP 443 for API and heartbeat.
  - Permit outbound from appliance to Redwood control plane: TCP 443 to redwood egress IPs (we will provide static IPs for production).

- Model inference/data plane (gRPC/HTTP)
  - If using VPC peering: allow private CIDR routing between Redwood VPC subnets and your application subnets; no additional NAT required.
  - If using PrivateLink: allow TCP 443 from appliance to customer NLB IPs and ensure TLS passthrough.

- KV cache and metrics endpoints
  - Outbound to s3-compatible storage endpoints for shard dumps and to our metrics collector over TCP 443.

- DNS and certs
  - Appliance must resolve redwood-managed FQDNs; ensure DNS is reachable from DMZ.
  - If you want to manage certs, we will provide CSR tooling and a cert rotation schedule (recommended 90 days).

- NAT/egress considerations
  - For staging, FQDN allowlist is fine. Production requires static egress IPs; if you have strict egress we will test via a short window first.

Attachments: short_firewall_checklist.txt (inline below)

Short checklist (copyable):
1) Open TCP 443 inbound to appliance management IP from Pegasus ops team.
2) Allow outbound TCP 443 to redwood-ctrl-1.redwood.ai and redwood-telemetry.redwood.ai.
3) Provide DNS resolution for redwood-managed FQDNs from DMZ.
4) Confirm whether you will host NLB for PrivateLink; if yes, share ARN and listener ports.

Happy to expand any item on the call.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team,

A few security preflight asks from our side to keep the deployment on the fast path: 

- SOC2 evidence: please share the contact for your compliance lead. We will provide a short evidence checklist specific to network segmentation and key management.
- Key handling: during staging, Pegasus should provide a test KMS endpoint and a non-production key. For production we will integrate with your KMS using the agreed KMS role.
- Logging and audit: confirm whether Pegasus requires centralized forwarding of audit logs from the appliance. If yes, provide the collector endpoint and auth method (TLS client cert vs token).
- Pen test window: schedule a 2-hour penetration validation after staging cutover; Redwood will coordinate but Pegasus must grant temporary lift for scanning IPs.

Action items before Tue 4/13 sync: 
- Pegasus: please attach a contact for the compliance lead and confirm whether you will host an NLB for PrivateLink.
- Redwood: we will circulate the short SOW amendment for the on-prem install (PEGA-2027-0410) and a proposed egress IP list for production.

Attachments: pegasus_sow_v2.docx

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
